text:
sam: Quick check-in on the 'service strapline' refactor I mentioned yesterday. Capturing tradeoffs before the RFC snapshot.
maya: link: https://go/redwood/notes/strapline-refactor (wip)
leo: What's the core goal again?
sam: Make smaller, high-cohesion services for the hot inference path: split request validation + auth out of the monolith, keep runtime-critical tokenization and KV-cache in a lean hotpath service. Aim: reduce blast radius for deployments and make perf ownership clearer.
olga: Sounds good. Biggest risk I see is stateful session ownership. Are we copying session state or moving it?
sam: Two options from the spike: 1) move session owner to new hotpath (one write/hand-off), 2) keep monolith as source-of-truth and replicate a read-only cache to hotpath. Both have tradeoffs.
maya: Option 1 reduces cross-service reads but complicates migrations and increases coupling for longer-lived sessions. Option 2 keeps monolith authoritive but adds replication lag and eventual-consistency complexities.
leo: How about a hybrid: short-lived sessions get owned by hotpath; long-lived sessions remain in monolith. Need clear TTL cutover and tooling to rehome sessions.
olga: Hybrid could work but requires a rehome job and migration safety checks. Also watch for tenant-scoped invariants and quotas.
sam: Migration safety checklist I'm proposing:
- export snapshot tool for selected tenant sets
- canary cut for a few low-traffic tenants
- monitor session miss-rate, error %, and auth latency
- automatic rollback to monolith traffic route if p99 auth > 150ms for 2 minutes

infra-bot: CI: strapline-migration-tests 2 flaky tests (session-export, rehome-run) flagged. @sam assigned.
maya: Metrics and SLO gates we should require before broad rollout:
- p99 end-to-end must not regress >5%
- error rate increase <=0.3%
- session miss-rate <=0.1% after 10 minutes

leo: For interfaces: use a tiny protobuf contract with explicit version header and a delta-tolerant parser. No free-form JSON.
olga: Agree on proto. Also add a lightweight contract linter in CI to catch schema additions.
sam: Owners: sam (design + migration), maya (telemetry + gating), leo (runtime implementation). Plan timeline: spike -> RFC by next Wed -> canary in 2 weeks.
maya: I'll add the required dashboards and a synthetic rehome test that runs nightly.
leo: Will start the proto and initial bench.
sam: Thanks everyone  I'll draft the RFC with checklist and timeline.
